title: Reading distance–time graphs
keyIdea: On a distance–time graph, flat means stopped, steeper means faster, and the gradient is the speed.

kid: A distance–time graph shows how far you are from the start at each moment. Time goes across. Distance goes up.
A flat line means you have stopped. A line going up means you are moving away. A steeper line means faster. A line going down means you are coming back.
adult: The gradient of a distance–time graph is the speed: distance ÷ time for that section. A straight line means a steady speed.
Average speed for the whole trip = total distance ÷ total time, including stops. A curved line means the speed is changing; the gradient of the tangent gives the speed at that moment.

familyTip: Sketch a graph of your walk to school: where did you stop, and where did you hurry?

practice.prompt: A flat line on a distance–time graph means…
practice.explain: No change in distance: not moving.

practice.prompt: A cyclist rides {d} km in {t} hours at a steady speed. What is the speed in km/h?
A line rises from 0 to {d} m in {t} s. What is its gradient (the speed in m/s)?
Which line shows the fastest movement?
practice.explain: The steepest line covers the most distance per unit of time.

pool.prompt: A walk: {a} km in 1 hour, a 30-minute stop, then {b} km in 1 hour. What is the average speed in km/h for the whole 2.5 hours?
A line sloping down towards the time axis means…
pool.hint: The distance from the start is shrinking.

pool.prompt: A section rises {d} km in {t} minutes. What is the speed in km per minute?
A curve that gets steeper and steeper shows…
At a steady {v} m/s for {t} s, how far do you go, in metres?
How do you find the speed from a straight section?
The graph is flat from minute {a} to minute {b}. How long was the stop, in minutes?

visual.caption: Drag along the graph or press Play. Watch the walker: flat means stopped, steep means fast, down means going home.
